title: GOD CANNOT LIE, HIS PROMISES NEVER FAIL
text: Beloved, before we go into this word and this time of prayer, I want you to do something for me. Share this. Share this with someone who is standing on a promise right now. Share this with someone whose faith has been tested, whose hope has been deferred, whose night has been long. Share this with someone who needs to be reminded that the God who spoke has not forgotten what he said. Send this to that brother, that sister, that friend who is about to give up on the promise. Because what is going to happen in this place today, in this word, in this prayer is going to shift atmospheres, ignite faith, and cause men and women to rise from the ashes of disappointment into the confidence of absolute trust in the living God. Share it now and then come back because we're about to go deep this morning. Now lift your hands wherever you are. Lift your hands and let's just take a moment to acknowledge him. Father, we thank you. We thank you for the gift of another morning. We thank you that we did not wake up this morning by our own power, by our own metabolism, by the beating of our own hearts. We woke up because you are a God of covenant. You are a God of faithfulness. Your mercies are new every morning and great is your faithfulness. Lord, we ask that before we say anything, before a single syllable is released into the atmosphere this morning, that your spirit will take absolute charge. that the Holy Ghost will be the preacher, the prayer leader, the intercessor, and the one who ministers to every heart. Father, let no one leave this place the same. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen. Now, open your Bibles. I want you to go with me to the book of Numbers, chapter 23, and I want to read to you from verse 19. Numbers 23:19. The word of God says, and I want you to read it with me, God is not a man that he should lie, nor a son of man that he should repent. Has he said and will he not do? Or has he spoken and will he not make it good? Now, somebody shout hallelujah. Because right there in that one verse is the foundation of everything I want to say to you this morning. God is not a man. God is not a man. The Bible is drawing a very deliberate distinction. a very intentional contrast between the nature of men and the nature of God. It is telling us something about the character, the essence, the very DNA of the Almighty. And the key thing it anchors on, the key attribute it highlights is this. God cannot lie. Now I want you to understand why this is so significant. You see, we are living in a generation where the word of men has become unreliable. We are living in a time where promises are made and promises are broken. where covenants are signed and covenants are violated, where agreements are reached and agreements are abandoned. We live in a world where the currency of a man's word has depreciated almost to the point of worthlessness. And because we live in that world, we bring that mentality, that disappointment, that scarred perception into our relationship with God. And we begin to read his promises with the same skepticism with which we read the promises of men. But the Bible is screaming at us this morning. God is not a man. The inability to lie is not simply a moral choice that God makes. I want you to understand this deeply. God does not simply choose not to lie the way a righteous man chooses not to lie. No, God cannot lie. The word in Titus 1:2 says, "God who cannot lie, promised." The Greek there carries the idea of absolute impossibility. It is not within the scope of his nature. It is outside the boundaries of his character. Lying would require God to act in a way that is fundamentally contrary to who he is. And God cannot be contrary to himself. God is truth. Jesus said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life." John 14:6, "Not I am a truth, not I speak truth, I am the truth." Truth is not just something God produces. Truth is something God is. Which means when God speaks, what comes out of his mouth is an extension of his nature and his nature cannot fail. Now listen to me. Isaiah 55-11 says, "So shall my word be that goes forth from my mouth. It shall not return to me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing for which I sent it." That word from the mouth of God goes out with an assignment. It goes out with a mission. It goes out with a divine mandate and it will not return until that mandate has been fulfilled. This means that every promise God has ever spoken over your life, every word he has ever dropped into your spirit, every prophetic declaration that has been released into your atmosphere, every scripture that the Holy Ghost has ever quickened to your heart is not idle words. Those words are working. Those words are on assignment. Those words are even now as I speak to you accomplishing what they were sent to accomplish. Now, let me slow down here because I want to talk to someone specifically. Someone is listening to me this morning and you have a promise. You received it years ago. It might have come through a prophetic word. It might have come through the scripture. It might have come through a dream, a vision, an impression so strong in your spirit that you knew beyond any shadow of doubt that God had spoken. And you held that promise. You wrote it in your journal. You rehearsed it in your heart. But time passed. Months turned into years. Years turned into what feels like an eternity. And the visible reality around you does not match the invisible promise that was given to you. And the enemy has come like he always comes whispering into your ear. Maybe God didn't say it. Maybe you misheard. Maybe it was just your emotions. Maybe it was just your desire. Because if God said it, surely by now it would have manifested. And I need you to know this morning that voice is a liar. Hear me. God cannot lie. Which means if God said it, it is true right now. Not when it manifests, it is already true. The promise is true before the manifestation appears. That's what faith is. Hebrews 11:1. Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. Faith is not waiting for evidence before it believes. Faith is the evidence. Faith is the substance. Faith treats the promise as already accomplished because the one who made the promise cannot lie. And if he cannot lie, then the promise is as real and as tangible as anything your physical eyes can see. Now, let me take you somewhere in scripture. I want to take you to Abraham, Romans chapter 4. I love this text. This is one of the most powerful treatises on faith and promise in the entire New Testament. Romans 4:17:1. Look at what Paul says about Abraham. It says, "Abraham believed in God who gives life to the dead and calls those things which do not exist as though they did." And then he says, "Who contrary to hope in hope believed so that he became the father of many nations according to what was spoken." Contrary to hope in hope believed. I want you to sit in that phrase for a moment. Contrary to hope, meaning at the natural, visible, empirical level, there was no basis for hope. Everything around Abraham said impossible. His body was as good as dead. He was about a hundred years old. Sarah's womb had never been active. She had never conceived in her life. The evidence, the medical evidence, the biological evidence, the natural evidence, all scream, "This promise cannot happen." But the Bible says, "Contrary to hope, in hope believed." Contrary to what his eyes could see, contrary to what logic dictated, contrary to what experience suggested, Abraham found a hope that was not anchored in natural circumstances. He found a hope that was anchored in the character of God. And look at verse 20. He did not waver at the promise of God through unbelief, but was strengthened in faith giving glory to God. He did not waver. He did not stagger. The word in the original language is he did not judge between two things. He did not stand in the middle looking at the promise and looking at the problem trying to decide which one was more real. He made a decision. He's settled in his heart. God said it. That is the end of the conversation. And notice what happened in his spirit. He was strengthened in faith giving glory to God. There is a glory that belongs to God before the manifestation. There is a praise that is prophetic. There is a worship that is not responsive but declarative. It is saying God even before I can see it, even before it has shown up in my body, in my bank account, in my marriage, in my ministry, in my family, I give you glory because I know who you are. I know you cannot lie. I know your word is settled in heaven even before it is settled on earth. And then verse 21, being fully convinced that what he had promised, he was also able to perform. fully convinced not partially convinced not 80% fully completely wholly persuaded can you say this morning I am fully persuaded that what God has promised he's also able to perform because that conviction that settled unshakable confidence in the faithfulness of God is what moves the hand of heaven now I want to shift I want to talk about something very important and I want you to follow me carefully We need to understand why promises seem to be delayed. Because if God cannot lie, if his word always accomplishes his purpose, why does it seem like some promises are taking too long? I want to give you several handles on this. The first thing I want to say is this. God operates in times and seasons, not just in instantaneous moments. Ecclesiastes 3:1 says, "To everything there is a season, a time for every purpose under heaven." God is not just concerned with the what of his promise. He is concerned with the when and the how and the context in which the promise arrives. Because the promise arriving at the wrong time without the right preparation in you can actually damage you rather than bless you. God in his wisdom holds some promises in heaven. Not because he has forgotten them, but because he's preparing you to be able to carry and sustain what he's about to release. Think about Joseph. Genesis 37, Joseph has a dream. God shows him that he will be a ruler, that nations will bow before him, that even his family will bow before him. He is 17 years old. And what happens next? His brothers throw him in a pit. He's sold into slavery. He ends up in Egypt. He serves faithfully in Portifer's house. And then a lying woman gets him thrown in prison. Now if you did not know the end of the story, you would look at Joseph's life and say that is a man whose promise has failed. Where is the dream? Where is the ruling? Where is the bowing? He is in a prison cell. He has been betrayed, forgotten, lied about, thrown away. But here is what you must understand. Every single thing that happened to Joseph was not a detour from the promise. Every single thing that happened to Joseph was a part of the roots to the promise. The pit was preparation. Slavery was preparation. Prison was preparation. The misinterpretation, the betrayal, the forgetting, it was all preparation. And at exactly the right moment, Genesis 41, Pharaoh has a dream. And overnight, Joseph goes from the prison to the palace. And every promise God had spoken over that young man came to pass. Not one word failed. Not one word. Because God cannot lie. The second thing I want to say about delayed promises is this. The enemy fights the promise. This is something we must understand as kingdom people. We are not in a neutral universe. We are in a battlefield. There is an adversary who has had the prophecy over your life, who has read the promises in your Bible, who knows what God has ordained for you and he fights it. Daniel chapter 10, Daniel prays and the angel of the Lord shows up 21 days later. And the angel says to Daniel, "From the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words. From day one, the answer was dispatched." But then he says, "But the prince of the kingdom of Pesha withtood me 21 days." There was a supernatural conflict over the delivery of that answer. And this is why Paul tells us in Ephesians 6 to put on the whole armor of God that we may be able to stand against the ws, the strategies, the methodologies of the devil. Because the enemy's primary strategy against a child of God who is standing on a promise is this. Make the delay feel like denial. Make the waiting feel like rejection. Make the silence of heaven feel like the absence of God. If he can get you to interpret your circumstances through the lens of disappointment rather than through the lens of the faithfulness of God, then he has won the battle without firing a single shot because you will do his job for him. You will let go of the promise. But I declare to you this morning, you shall not let go. You shall hold on. You shall stand. You shall keep your grip on the word of God even when everything around you suggests that word has been cancelled because God cannot lie. And what he has promised, he will do. Let me take you to one more text. Joshua 21:45. After all the battles, after all the journeys, after all the wars to possess the promised land, the Bible says this, "Not a word failed of any good thing which the Lord had spoken to the house of Israel." All came to pass. All came to pass. Not some, not most, not the convenient ones. All came to pass. every word, every promise, every covenant declaration, all of it in God's economy, the fail rate on his promises is zero. Absolute zero. It has never happened that God spoke a promise and that promise did not come to pass. Never. Not once in all of eternity, in all of human history, has God ever made a promise that he did not keep. And if that is the God you serve and it is, then why would you live in fear? Why would you accept defeat? Why would you bow your head to the lies of the enemy and say, "This is my portion." No. Stand up in the revelation of who your God is, in the revelation of the absolute reliability of his word and say, "If God said it, I will see it. If God promised it, I will possess it. If God ordained it, it will come to pass." Now, there is something else I want to address, and this is very important for this morning's prayer time. There is a role that you play in the fulfillment of God's promises. God's promises are not passive. They are not automatic. Many of God's promises are conditional. They have conditions attached to them. And many of his promises, while unconditional in their nature, still require your active participation, your agreement, your declaration. Hebrews 4:2, he speaks about the children of Israel who had the promise and died in the wilderness without possessing it. And the Bible gives us the reason. It says, "But the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in those who heard it." The promise was real. The word was true. God was not lying. But the word was not mixed with faith. And a promise unmixed with faith, unactivated by agreement, uninforced by prayer, becomes a potential that never becomes an actual. This is why prayer matters. This is why we are here this morning. Prayer is not us trying to convince God to do something he's reluctant to do. Prayer is us activating, enforcing, and calling forth what God has already ordained. Prayer is us saying, "Father, what you have spoken over my life, what your word declares concerning me, what your covenant guarantees, I am calling it forth right now. I am mixing faith with this promise. I am declaring it into the atmosphere. I am enforcing it against every opposition. And this is the spirit of prayer I want to lead you in right now. So let's build from the word into the place of prayer. And I want you to lift your voice with me. I want you to be aggressive this morning. I want you to understand that the messages of God are new this morning. Not just for celebration, but for enforcement. Let us pray. Father, we come before you this morning with confidence. Not confidence in ourselves, CONFIDENCE IN YOU. NOT CONFIDENCE in our righteousness, but in your faithfulness. Hebrews 10:23 says, "Hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering. For he who promised is faithful." We declare this morning, you are faithful. You have always been faithful in every generation, in every season, in every circumstance. You have always been faithful. And we anchor ourselves in that faithfulness right now. Lord, we thank you that your word is settled. Psalm 119 to 89. Forever. Oh Lord, your word is settled in heaven. Even when we cannot see the manifestation on earth, your word is already settled in heaven. It is accomplished. It is finished. It is done. And we call it from heaven to earth this morning. We call it from the eternal into the temporal. We call it from the invisible into the visible. Let your word that is settled in heaven become tangible reality in our lives in this season in Jesus name. Now lift your voice and pray this. Father I stand on your word this morning. I stand on your promise. I will not be moved by what I see. I will not be moved by what I feel. I will not be moved by the noise of the enemy or the logic of my circumstances. Your word says you cannot lie. Your word says your promises never fail. And I take you at your word this morning. I take you at your word. Now I want to get prophetic in this prayer. I want you to follow me aggressively. Lift your voice and begin to declare. Every promise that has been delayed in my life, I declare that the time of delay is over. Every word that God has spoken over me, I declare that this is the season of its fulfillment. The Bible says in 2 Corinthians 1:20 that all the promises of God in Christ Jesus are yes and in him amen. Yes and amen. Every promise, not some. Every promise. If God said healing, it is yes. If God said restoration, it is yes. If God said promotion, it is yes. If God said your children shall be saved, it is yes. If God said your marriage shall be restored, it is yes. Every single promise over my life is yes in Christ Jesus. and amen to the glory of God through us. Now, I want to pray for your specific situations. I want to call them out because I believe the spirit of God is moving right now. Somebody here is waiting for a financial breakthrough. You have held on to the promise that God will be your provider. You have given. You have sacrificed. You have trusted. And there are moments when you wonder if it is working. I declare over you this morning, Philippians 4:19 is true. My God shall supply all your needs according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus. That is not a suggestion. That is not a possibility. That is a covenant declaration from the mouth of God himself. And since he cannot lie, your supply is guaranteed. I declare that the windows of heaven are opening over your life. I declare that divine ideas, divine connections, divine opportunities, and supernatural provisions are flowing into your life right now in Jesus name. Now pray with your mouth. Open your mouth and declare, "I shall not lack." God is my provider. His supply is not limited by the economy. His supply is not limited by the market. His supply is not limited by my situation. His supplies from his riches in glory, not his riches in the bank, not his riches on the stock exchange, his riches in glory, and his glory is inexhaustible. Therefore, my supply is inexhaustible. I shall have more than enough. I shall be a blessing to nations. I shall lend and not borrow. I shall be the head and not the tail. I shall be above and not beneath. This is the word of the Lord over my life and it shall not return void in Jesus name. Now somebody else is standing on a promise for health and healing. You have been through a diagnosis that shook you. You have been through a medical report that tried to speak death over you. You have been through physical suffering that has been prolonged, that has been painful, that has tried to steal your faith. But hear me. Isaiah 53:5 says, "By his stripes you were healed where, past tense, it is accomplished. Calvary settled the matter of your healing. The blood of Jesus Christ that was shed on that cross paid the full price not just for your sins, but for your sicknesses. Not just for your iniquities, but for your infirmities. And what was bought at the cross is yours this morning. I speak healing into every sick body right now. I speak healing to every broken organ. I speak healing to every diagnosis that has been released against the children of God. Cancer, hear the word of the Lord. You have no authority over the child of God. Disease, hear the word of the Lord. You are under the blood. Sickness, you must bow to the name of Jesus Christ. In the name of Jesus, every mountain of sickness in the lives of those praying with us this morning, be removed and be cast into the sea. Be gone. You have no place here. God cannot lie. And his word says we are healed. So healing manifest now in Jesus mighty name. Now lift your voice and declare I am healed by the stripes of Jesus. My body is a temple of the Holy Ghost and the Holy Ghost does not dwell in ruins. He is restoring every part of me. He is regenerating, rebuilding and renewing my physical body. Every organ shall function at the level of supernatural design. Every cell in my body shall align with the word of God. I walk in divine health because God cannot lie and he has promised me healing in Jesus name. Now I want to pray for the unmarried the ones who are standing on a promise for a life partner. I know this is a sensitive area. I know this is an area where the weight has been painful where comparisons have been tormenting where loneliness has sometimes been overwhelming. But hear what the word of God says. Proverbs 18:22 says, "He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the Lord." The favor of God is attached to that covenant. And Psalm 37:4 says, "Delight yourself also in the Lord, and he shall give you the desires of your heart, the desires of your heart, not the desires of someone else's heart. the specific desires that God himself planted in you. I declare over every single person trusting God for a covenant partner. Your waiting is not in vain. God is not withholding from you out of stinginess or oversight. He is preparing both you and the one he has ordained for you. He is working in the scene and in the unseen. He's arranging, aligning, orchestrating and at the right time the right person will show up. Not just someone but the god orained, God confirmed, spirit approved person who will be a true complement to your destiny in Jesus name. Now declare this with your mouth. God has not forgotten me. My time of waiting is coming to an end. The one God has for me is coming. No weapon of loneliness shall continue to break me. No spirit of fear shall make me settle for less than God's best. I am patient. I am prepared. And I am waiting with expectation. God cannot lie. He promised and he will bring it to pass in Jesus' name. Hallelujah. Now, let me pray for the ministers of the gospel. The ones who are in ministry, some in full-time ministry, some in marketplace ministry, some who are still in the place of preparation, waiting to be launched. God gave you a mandate. God showed you a vision. God put a burning in your spirit that you could not explain, that you could not manufacture, that came from nowhere except from heaven. And in the years since that mandate was given, there have been times of doubt, times of asking, did I really hear God? Is this really what I am supposed to do? Because the doors seem closed, the resources seem absent, the platform seems invisible, and the people don't seem to be coming. Hear me. God is not mocked. What he has ordained, no man can abort. Isaiah 46 to10 says, "My counsel shall stand and I will do all my pleasure, all his pleasure, including the mandate he placed in you, he will accomplish it. He will bring it to pass. The doors that need to open will open. The resources that need to come will come. The connections that need to be made will be made. The platform that needs to be given will be given. Not because you are great, but because God cannot lie and he has spoken. I release you into your purpose this morning. I declare prophetically that chains are being broken off your destiny. I declare that you are entering a new phase of acceleration. What took 10 years before will now happen in one season. I declare divine speed over your ministry. I declare open doors before you that no man can shut. I declare the right fathers, the right mentors, the right collaborators are coming into alignment around you. Rise up child of God. Your moment is here. The Lord your God is with you in Jesus' name. Now, let me go back to prayer because we are not done. We have more ground to take. Lift your voice again with me. Father, we thank you because this morning we have rehearsed your faithfulness. We have reminded ourselves, not you because you do not need reminding. We have reminded ourselves of who you are. You are the God who cannot lie. You are the God whose promises never fail. You are the God who was faithful to Abraham, faithful to Joseph, faithful to Moses, faithful to Joshua, faithful to David, faithful to every generation that has trusted in you. And Lord, we are declaring this morning, you are faithful to us. You will be faithful to us in this season. Every promise that has been in the pipeline, Lord, we ask that you accelerate the delivery. We ask for supernatural speed. We ask for the unusual, unexpected manifestation of your word in our lives this season. Not next year, not in 10 years, this season. And I want to address the enemy directly. I want you to lift your voice and declare this enemy, hear me this morning. You have tried to make me doubt. You have whispered lies. You have painted pictures of failure and disappointment and permanent delay. But I am not deceived. My God cannot lie. His word stands. His promises are immovable. You have no authority to cancel what God has ordained. You have no power to delay beyond what God permits. And in the name of Jesus Christ, every satanic hold on my promises is broken right now. Every demonic resistance to my breakthrough is shattered. Every wall that you have erected between me and my destiny, I pull it down in the name of Jesus. The Bible says in 2 Corinthians 10:4, "The weapons of our warfare are not cannal but mighty in God for pulling down strongholds. I take up the weapons of the spirit right now. The word of God, the blood of Jesus, the name above every name, and I pull down every stronghold that has been keeping my promises captive. I declare they are free. I declare they are released. I declare they are coming to manifestation in Jesus name." Now pray for your family. I want you to pray for the people connected to you because when God makes a promise, it is often not just about you. It touches everyone in your circle, everyone in your bloodline, everyone in your sphere of influence. Father, I bring my family before you this morning. Every member of my household, I stand in the gap for them. I declare that the covenant I have with you extends to cover them. Acts 16:31, believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and you will be saved, you and your household. I take that promise for every family member who is yet to come to you. I declare that eyes that are spiritually blind shall be opened. Ears that cannot hear, your voice shall begin to hear. Hearts that have been hardened shall be softened by the fire of your love. Prodigals are coming home. Rebellious children are turning back. Lost family members are finding their way because God cannot lie and he has promised salvation to my household. And for those in my family who are already in the kingdom, I declare advancement. I declare promotion. I declare divine health and protection over every member of my household. No weapon formed against my family shall prosper. No sickness, no accident, no spirit of death, no generational curse, no demonic assignment, nothing that has been formed against my family shall prosper because the covenant of God is over us. The blood of Jesus is on our doorpost. We are covered. We are protected. We are blessed in Jesus name. Let me prophesy something now and I want you to receive this with faith. I see somebody watching this and there is a specific promise you have been carrying for more than 5 years. You have held that promise quietly. You have not told many people because you did not want the ridicle. You have not broadcast it because the delay has been embarrassing. But you have held it in your heart. You have returned to it on your darkest nights. You have wept over it in secret prayer. God knows about that promise. God knows about that prayer. And he's saying to you this morning, it is not cancelled. It is not forgotten. It is not rejected. It is on its way. This season, this season, you will begin to see the first fruits of that long-held promise. What has seemed dormant is about to bust into bloom. What has seemed dead is about to resurrect. What has seemed impossible is about to become your testimony. Because God cannot lie and he has never once abandoned a promise that he has made. Now I need you to make a declaration one more time. Lift your voice and say it like you mean it. I believe God. I believe every word he has spoken over my life. I believe his promises are yes and amen. I believe that what he started he will complete. I believe that what he promised he will perform. I believe that my best days are ahead and not behind. I believe that the manifestations I have been waiting for are coming. I believe not in myself, not in my circumstances, but in the faithfulness of the God who cannot lie. And I will not give up. I will not throw away my confidence. I will hold my declaration of faith steady until I see every single promise of God manifest in my life in Jesus name. Hallelujah. Father, we seal this morning's prayer. We seal this morning's word with thanksgiving. We take everything that has been spoken this morning, everything that has been declared, every prophetic word that has been released, every prayer that has gone up from the hearts of those praying with us. And we place it before your throne. We ask that your angels go on assignment. We ask that the word that has been sown this morning bring forth a harvest 30, 60, 100fold. We ask that faith has been steed, that hope has been renewed, that expectation has been restored. Lord, let the testimonies come. Let them come quickly. Let the children of God who have been waiting arise and say, "I saw the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living." Psalm 27-13. I would have lost heart unless I had believed that I would see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living. Not in the hereafter, not in eternity, in the land of the living. right here, right now, in this season, in this generation. Let them see your goodness, Lord. Let them testify of your faithfulness. Let your name be glorified. We give you all the honor. We give you all the praise. We give you all the glory. For you are worthy. Worthy of every ounce of trust, every measure of faith, every declaration of praise that we release this morning. You are worthy because you cannot lie. Your promises never fail. Your word endures forever. Your faithfulness extends to all generations. And we are the generation that declares, "God is faithful. God is faithful. God is faithful in Jesus' name." Amen. Amen. Amen. Go and carry this confidence with you today. When the enemy comes to whisper doubt, remind him my God cannot lie. When circumstances scream impossibility, remind yourself his word never returns void. When the wait feels too long, anchor yourself in the testimony of Abraham, of Joseph, of every man and woman who held on to God's promise and live to see his fulfillment. You will not be the exception. You will be the testimony. You will be the evidence that God is still faithful. God bless you richly this
